scope.selection: Deterministic metadata hash order, cached native TPF and PRF, unique parent scenes; no detector result selection
scope.preflight_reason: Only one quality-zero cadence with finite pointing, below the frozen minimum100
scope.population: Five selected K-dwarf sources; not a representative M/K population
scope.depth_convention: Nominal radius-ratio squared; limb-darkened exposure-integrated peak losses saved separately

preparation.null_protocol: 128 calibration and128 held independent sign-block realizations per source/operator/method, separately for1-day and2-day blocks; nominal5% plus-one rank threshold
preparation.interpretation: Amplitude retention improves, but blind recovery gains are modest and held false-alarm control is not uniform. Joint known-clock amplitude near1 is an algebraic property, not proof of increased information.

native_detector.limits: Five scenes, one period-duration-phase per scene, two nominal depths; original controls only, no calibrated native-detector FPR

pixel_budget.model: Live integration=INT_TIME*NUM_FRM; Poisson variance=rate/live; read variance=NUM_FRM*READNOIS^2/live^2. Propagate fixed extraction weights squared. Signed unexplained variance retained.
limits: Read component follows mission header model; not a measurement of its fraction of observed variability
Target and neighbor assignments are conditional on imperfect scene/PRF/astrometry
Scene fractional absolute residuals4.46–12.66%; budget does not close
No optimal extraction, photon-limit or irreducible information-bound claim

conclusions: 46/200 is a conditional detectability screen, not a physical maximum.
The selected0.5-day coarse filter still loses long-transit amplitude; original prepared flux remains available to the physical fit.
A one-day window and joint initial scoring improve transfer but do not create missing photons or eliminate random read noise.
The experimental fixed PRF operator is not an improvement to adopt: two modest formal-noise gains, two modest losses, one severe amplification.
All four full-detector configurations have identical recovery on this pilot.
Zero40–300ppm recovery over45days cannot establish impossibility over full-mission baselines.

next_method.proposal: Joint sparse spline nuisance and transit scoring from the initial search, or duration-aware detrending with empirically measured transfer
tools: Empirical full-search null maxima and injection recovery
gates: Recalibrate tails on independent controls and fresh source clusters
Use full available mission baselines and physically host-consistent probes
